title: Route Tables
explanation: A route table contains a set of rules (routes) that determine where network traffic from your subnet or gateway is directed. Each subnet must be associated with a route table, which controls the routing for that subnet.
analogy: Route tables are like road signs at intersections — they tell traffic which direction to go based on the destination address.
keyPoints: Every subnet must be associated with exactly one route table
The main route table is automatically assigned to subnets without explicit association
Routes are evaluated using longest prefix match
Local route (VPC CIDR) is always present and cannot be removed

examKeywords.definition: A set of routing rules that determine where network traffic is directed based on destination IP address.

commonMistakes: Modifying the main route table instead of creating custom route tables for specific subnets
Not understanding longest prefix match — more specific routes take priority
